title: Which two shapes pass both the fold test and the turn test?
description: A plus sign with four equal arms and a triangle with three equal sides are folded and then turned about the centre. Each one has fold lines and a turn smaller than a full turn that fits. The video breaks the idea that a shape must look balanced to pass; only the fold test and the turn test decide.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape has both kinds of symmetry when it passes the fold test and also fits after a turn smaller than a full turn. Watch for students who pick a shape because it looks balanced without folding or turning it.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (section 9.2, second block)
video_script.why: The child learns to choose a shape by testing it twice, once with a fold and once with a turn about the centre.
video_script.substitution: Draw the shape, fold it along every line that might work, then turn it about its centre and watch where it fits.
video_script.anchor: two shapes drawn on paper, a plus sign with four equal arms and a triangle with three equal sides
video_script.payoff_line: A plus sign and a triangle with three equal sides pass both tests

final_answer.value: plus sign: 4 lines, 4 angles; triangle with 3 equal sides: 3 lines, 3 angles
final_answer.spoken: a plus sign with four equal arms has four lines and four angles of symmetry, and a triangle with three equal sides has three lines and three angles

never_show: a circle or a square as an answer
a leaning parallelogram accepted as having both kinds of symmetry
maths_rules: plus sign with 4 equal arms: fold lines are the vertical, the horizontal and the 2 slanting lines, so 4 lines of symmetry
360 / 4 = 90, so the plus sign fits after 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees: 4 angles of symmetry
triangle with 3 equal sides: one fold line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side, so 3 lines of symmetry
360 / 3 = 120, so the triangle fits after 120, 240 and 360 degrees: 3 angles of symmetry
the question excludes the circle and the square; neither answer is one of them
both shapes have a turn smaller than 360 degrees that fits, so both have rotational symmetry as well as reflection symmetry
video_script.design: One idea: test a shape twice, by folding and by turning. Two shapes drawn one after the other on the same paper. The fold lines are teal and the turns are amber.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two empty sheets of paper side by side; a fold arrow on the first and a turn arrow on the second; the words not a circle, not a square appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.fold: a fold arrow appears on the first sheet and a turn arrow on the second
marks.ask: the words not a circle, not a square appear under the sheets

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about drawing shapes that match themselves in two ways.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>One way is to fold the shape, and the other way is to turn it.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The shapes must not be a circle or a square. Which shapes can you draw that pass both tests?

beats.on_screen: the sheets hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a paper shape folds along a dashed teal line and the halves cover each other; then the shape turns about a red dot and fits its outline again; a full turn is marked on the circle of turns

marks.line: a shape folds along a dashed teal line and the halves cover each other
marks.angle: the shape turns about a red dot and fits its outline again
marks.full: a full turn is marked on the circle of turns and glows

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A fold line where both halves cover each other exactly is called a line of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>A turn that makes a shape look exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='full'/>A full turn always fits, so three hundred sixty degrees is always an angle of symmetry. We need a smaller turn that fits too.

beats.on_screen: Given: two shapes wanted, neither a circle nor a square

marks.given: the words two shapes, not a circle, not a square are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, we need two shapes, and neither shape is a circle or a square.

beats.on_screen: To find: shapes with a fold line and a turn smaller than a full turn that fits

marks.find: the words fold line and smaller turn are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find shapes with a fold line and a turn smaller than a full turn.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, fold test: a plus sign with 4 equal arms is folded up and down, sideways and along both slanting lines; the halves match each time; 4 fold lines

marks.plus: a plus sign with four equal arms is drawn around a red centre dot
marks.fold: the plus sign folds four ways and the halves match each time
marks.lines: the four fold lines are drawn in teal

narration: <bookmark mark='plus'/>Step one, draw the plus sign with four equal arms.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Fold it up and down, sideways, and along both slanting lines. The halves match every time.
<bookmark mark='lines'/>The plus sign has four lines of symmetry, because four different folds work.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, turn test: 360 / 4 = 90; the plus sign turns 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees about the centre and fits each time; 4 angles

marks.quarter: the plus sign turns about its centre and fits after ninety degrees
marks.list: the turns 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees are listed in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='quarter'/>Step two, turn the plus sign about its centre. It fits after ninety degrees, because all four arms are equal.
<bookmark mark='list'/>It also fits after one hundred eighty and two hundred seventy degrees, and after the full turn.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, a triangle with 3 equal sides: 3 fold lines from corner to the middle of the opposite side; 360 / 3 = 120; turns 120, 240, 360 degrees

marks.tri: a triangle with three equal sides is drawn on a second sheet
marks.tfold: three teal fold lines run from each corner to the middle of the opposite side
marks.tturn: the equation 360 / 3 = 120 is written and the turns 120, 240 and 360 degrees are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step three, draw a triangle with three equal sides and three equal angles.
<bookmark mark='tfold'/>Fold it from each corner to the middle of the opposite side, and the halves match.
<bookmark mark='tturn'/>Three hundred sixty divided by three is one hundred twenty. The turns that fit are one hundred twenty, two hundred forty and three hundred sixty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: neither shape is a circle or a square; each folds onto itself; each fits after a turn smaller than a full turn

marks.check: the two shapes sit side by side and a tick appears for not a circle, not a square
marks.both: a teal tick for the fold and an amber tick for the turn appear on each shape

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. Neither shape is a circle or a square.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Each shape folds onto itself, and each fits after a turn smaller than a full turn.

beats.on_screen: Answer: plus sign: 4 lines, 4 angles; triangle with 3 equal sides: 3 lines, 3 angles

marks.counts: the counts for the plus sign are ticked off

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A plus sign and a triangle with three equal sides pass both tests.
<bookmark mark='counts'/>The plus sign has four lines and four angles of symmetry.
The triangle has three lines and three angles.
